You are a CODE CLEANUP reviewer focused on ONE angle: ALTITUDE (is each change implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile special-case bandaid?). Do not hunt for correctness bugs.

The diff under review is at: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/9fb5c597-ba1e-4046-8ada-d69e84b4f335/scratchpad/simplify_diff.txt

It adds Andes V5 CSR transport across 3 repos:
- andesim_abi (ABI header): /home/nick/work/andesim/include/hybrid/state_abi.h , state_abi_check.h
- andesim (driver+plugin): /home/nick/work/andesim/driver/state_diff.cpp , driver/state_diff_test.cpp , qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- hybrid_vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp , state_drain.hpp , and tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp

YOUR TASK: Check that each change sits at the right depth. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are the smell to look for. Candidates:
- The msp_bound/msp_base verify exclusion is a hardcoded name-match special-case in state_diff.cpp. Today, how is `mip` excluded (it has the same "hardware/platform-divergent, transport-but-do-not-verify" property)? Is mip excluded by simply NOT being in the compare list, while the Andes block excludes by an in-loop name check? If those two exclusion mechanisms differ, is the new one at the wrong altitude — should "transport-but-do-not-verify" be a property of the field list itself (e.g. a flag/tier in HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST) rather than a separate name-matching lambda? Weigh both: a 4th column in the X-macro vs the lambda. Give a recommendation.
- PMA is transported as arrays OUTSIDE the X-macro (separate loops in all 4 consumers) while scalars go through the X-macro. Is that split at the right altitude, or does it duplicate the "iterate + transport" shape 4 times? Could PMA ride the same mechanism, or is arrays-vs-scalars a real reason to keep them separate?
- The X-macro carries (field, addr, gdb_name). The plugin uses gdb_name, resume/drain use addr. Is anything resolved at the wrong layer?
- HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES gating is repeated as `if (flags & HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES)` in all 4 consumers — is that the right altitude (each consumer independently gates) or should it be centralized?

Read the actual files AND the existing mip-exclusion code to ground each finding. For each give: file, line, one-line summary, whether the current altitude is acceptable or should be generalized, your recommended deeper form, and the concrete cost of leaving it. Be decisive with a recommendation per finding. Return a concise bulleted list.

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 3 (Andes F0): append struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl, which
25	// grows the struct. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to 128 bytes/register.
26	// Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers check magic + version
27	// + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
28	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 3u
29	
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
32	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
33	// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
34	// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
35	// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
36	#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
37	
38	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
39	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
40	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
41	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
42	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
43	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
44	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
45	
46	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
47	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
48	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
49	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
50	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
51	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
52	
53	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
54	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
55	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
56	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
57	
58	// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
59	// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
60	// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
61	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
62	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
63	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
64	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
65	
66	// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
67	// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
68	// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
69	// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
70	// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
71	// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
72	// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
73	#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
74	  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \
75	  X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl")      \
76	  X(mclk_ctl,       0x7DF, "mclk_ctl")      \
77	  X(milmb,          0x7C0, "milmb")         \
78	  X(mdlmb,          0x7C1, "mdlmb")         \
79	  X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code")     \
80	  X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl")      \
81	  X(msp_bound,      0x7C7, "msp_bound")     \
82	  X(msp_base,       0x7C8, "msp_base")      \
83	  X(mcountermask_m, 0x7D1, "mcountermask_m")\
84	  X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb")          \
85	  X(jvt,            0x017, "jvt")           \
86	  X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode")
87	
88	// The Andes V5 machine/user CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI
89	// (boot-static memory system + extension config) plus the DSP overflow flag.
90	// Restored at resume, re-read at drain, and verified -- live only when
91	// HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is set. 13 scalar fields (above) + PMA = 31 * uint64_t.
92	struct hybrid_andes_csr {
93	#define HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
94	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD)
95	#undef HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD
96	  uint64_t pmacfg[HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM];
97	  uint64_t pmaaddr[HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM];
98	};
99	
100	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
101	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
102	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
103	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
104	  uint32_t magic;
105	  uint32_t version;
106	  uint32_t flags;
107	  uint32_t hart_id;
108	  uint64_t pc;
109	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
110	
111	  uint64_t gpr[32];
112	  uint64_t fpr[32];
113	
114	  uint64_t mstatus;
115	  uint64_t mepc;
116	  uint64_t mtvec;
117	  uint64_t mcause;
118	  uint64_t mtval;
119	  uint64_t mscratch;
120	  uint64_t medeleg;
121	  uint64_t mideleg;
122	  uint64_t mip;
123	  uint64_t mie;
124	  uint64_t mcycle;
125	  uint64_t minstret;
126	  uint64_t satp;
127	
128	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
129	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
130	
131	  uint64_t vstart;
132	  uint64_t vtype;
133	  uint64_t vl;
134	  uint64_t vlenb;
135	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
136	  uint64_t vxsat;
137	  uint64_t vxrm;
138	  uint64_t vcsr;
139	
140	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
141	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
142	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
143	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
144	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
145	  uint64_t fcsr;
146	
147	  // Andes machine-setup CSRs: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches,
148	  // mmisc_ctl (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. crt0 writes them once at
149	  // boot; transporting them keeps the cycle engine from resuming caches-off
150	  // (ResumeDriver has the full rationale). Drained by the plugin, restored by
151	  // ResumeDriver, but NOT re-read by StateDrain: they are boot-static and the
152	  // drained value is unused (no QEMU2 leg). Old state files carry 0 here
153	  // (reset value), which is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump.
154	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
155	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
156	
157	  // v3: Andes V5 CSR block (live when HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES). 31 * 8 = 248 bytes.
158	  struct hybrid_andes_csr andes;
159	
160	  uint8_t  reserved[64];  // zero-initialise on write; v3-compatible growth room
161	};
162	
163	#ifdef __cplusplus
164	}  // extern "C"
165	#endif
166	
167	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
168	
169	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H

content.text: Now let me read the state_diff.cpp (to find the mip exclusion mechanism), the plugin, and state_abi_check.h.
Let me read the vsim resume/drain files and the state_diff test to ground the PMP-vs-PMA and mip comparison.
Let me read the state_drain.hpp to see how it handles PMP and the existing passthrough pattern.

I have everything I need. All findings are grounded in the actual files.

## Altitude review: Andes V5 CSR transport

**1. `msp_bound`/`msp_base` verify exclusion -- in-loop name-match lambda**
- File/line: `driver/state_diff.cpp:92-97` (lambda) vs `mip` excluded by omission (no `cmp(r,"mip",...)` line exists anywhere; rationale comment at `:37-40`).
- Summary: `mip` is excluded by simply not appearing in the hand-written compare sequence; the Andes block, being X-macro-generated, can't "omit" a row so it adds a runtime `std::string(name)=="msp_bound"||...` filter inside the loop. The two mechanisms differ because one list is hand-written and one is generated -- that asymmetry is inherent, not a smell.
- Verdict: ACCEPTABLE altitude. Do NOT promote to a 4th X-macro column. "Verify-excluded" is a single-consumer property (only the verifier cares; plugin/resume/drain transport these two normally), and every other excluded CSR in this same file (mstatus, mtvec, mip, satp, pmp) has its verify policy decided locally in the verifier. A 4th column would lift a leaf concern into the shared contract and force edits to ~11 unrelated expansion sites across 3 repos that all ignore it.
- Cost of leaving: near-zero. Drift (renaming column 3) is caught loudly by `state_diff_test.cpp:334-342`. Two micro-polish options only: key the filter off the `addr` int or a `string_view` set instead of two `std::string` temporaries, and hoist to a local set if the exclusion list ever exceeds ~3 entries.

**2. PMA transported as arrays outside the X-macro (separate loops x5-6)**
- File/line: `state_abi.h:96-97`; loops in `hybrid_handoff.c:165-173,321-328`, `resume_driver.hpp:259-262`, `state_drain.hpp:119-124`, `state_diff.cpp:100-105`.
- Summary: the "iterate + transport PMA" shape is repeated per consumer, exactly mirroring the existing PMP banks (`resume_driver.hpp:184-187`, `hybrid_handoff.c:174-181`).
- Verdict: ACCEPTABLE altitude -- arrays-vs-scalars is a real reason. PMA is a homogeneous indexed bank, so it correctly follows the established PMP array pattern, not the scalar X-macro. Flattening into the macro would add 18 lines (16 addr + 2 cfg), lose `for`-loop indexing, and force hardcoded `"pmaaddr5"` label strings. The per-consumer loop duplication is inherent (different language/API per consumer: `find_reg` vs `read_reg64` vs `write_csr_tolerant` vs `cmp`) and already accepted for PMP.
- Cost of leaving: none structurally. One minor nit worth fixing: the even-CSR stride `0xBC0 + 2*i` is re-derived in 3 places (`resume_driver.hpp:262`, `state_drain.hpp:121`, `hybrid_handoff.c:167`). Add `HYBRID_PMA_CFG_CSR(i)`/`HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_CSR(i)` helper macros next to the existing `HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR` in the header to centralize the addressing.

**3. X-macro 3 columns (field, addr, gdb_name) -- plugin uses name, DMI uses addr**
- File/line: list at `state_abi.h:73-86`; name used at `hybrid_handoff.c:162` and `state_diff.cpp:97`; addr used at `resume_driver.hpp:253`, `state_drain.hpp:116`.
- Summary: the plugin resolves by gdbstub name (its API is name-keyed), resume/drain address CSRs by number (Debug Module is number-keyed). These are two genuine namespaces for the same CSR.
- Verdict: layering is CORRECT -- nothing is resolved at the wrong layer; the contract carrying both identifiers so each consumer picks its own is textbook right-altitude. One redundancy nit: column 3 equals `#field` (stringize of column 1) in all 13 rows today, so it is currently pure duplication and creates a silent-drop path -- a field rename that misses column 3 yields a stale gdb name -> NULL handle -> drains 0, which is indistinguishable from "engine lacks the CSR" (tolerant no-op), so verify still passes on 0==0.
- Cost of leaving: low but real (a missed-rename silently drops one CSR from transport with no loud failure). Either collapse column 3 to `#field` via a stringize helper to kill the drift path, or keep it as deliberate decoupling from QEMU's external naming -- in which case treat it as a watch-item. Not an altitude error, a DRY nit.

**4. `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` gated independently in each consumer**
- File/line: `resume_driver.hpp:252`, `state_drain.hpp:115`, `state_diff.cpp:95`; produced (set) at `hybrid_handoff.c:315-329`.
- Summary: each consumer independently does `if (flags & HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES)`.
- Verdict: RIGHT altitude. This is exactly the established `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V` pattern (`resume_driver.hpp:124,134,144`; `state_drain.hpp:77,84`; `state_diff.cpp:48,54`). The policy IS already centralized -- a single flag bit in the shared ABI; enforcement is necessarily per-consumer because the consumers live in 3 repos with no shared dispatch point. There is nothing to centralize into.
- Cost of leaving: none. Keep as-is.

**5. (Bonus, strongest altitude smell) `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` left as hand-maintained one-offs beside the new X-macro**
- File/line: struct fields `state_abi.h:154-155`; constants `resume_driver.hpp:60-61` + restore `:240-241`; plugin handles `hybrid_handoff.c:52-53` + resolve `:156-157` + drain `:308-309`.
- Summary: these are Andes machine-setup scalar CSRs identical in shape to the 13 X-macro entries, but they predate the macro, so they remain duplicated across every consumer by hand -- the exact "special case sitting beside the shared infrastructure that would absorb it" pattern. Note `msp_bound`/`msp_base` are also boot-static and not strictly verified yet live IN the macro (just verify-excluded), so "boot-static / not-verified" is not a real reason to keep mcache/mmisc out.
- Verdict: should be GENERALIZED -- fold both into `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` as two more lines, deleting their standalone struct fields, `kCsr` constants, plugin handles, and individual drain/restore lines.
- Cost of folding (not free, confirm first): they shift from unconditional to `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`-gated (practically equivalent -- a non-Andes stub reads 0 either way, and any core with mcache_ctl sets `has_andes`), and from not-re-read/not-verified to re-read + verified. The latter reverses a deliberate "boot-static, drained value unused" choice, so confirm they round-trip equal in a trap-free ROI (they almost certainly do) before folding; if there is a genuine reason to keep them restore-only, leave them but add a comment stating why they are excluded from the macro. Cost of leaving as-is: two CSRs' worth of consumer-drift risk that the v3 X-macro was specifically built to eliminate.

Net: bullets 1, 2, and 4 sit at the correct altitude and should stay; bullet 3 is correctly layered with a minor redundancy nit; bullet 5 (mcache/mmisc) is the one clear-cut generalization worth doing.
